items.name: gvisor
items.description: Application Kernel for Containers

readme.excerpt:
gVisor provides a strong layer of isolation between running applications and the host operating system. It is an application kernel that implements a [Linux-like interface][linux]. Unlike Linux, it is written in a memory-safe language (Go) and runs in userspace.

gVisor includes an [Open Container Initiative (OCI)][oci] runtime called runsc that makes it easy to work with existing container tooling. The runsc runtime integrates with Docker and Kubernetes, making it simple to run sandboxed containers.

gVisor is not a syscall filter (e.g. seccomp-bpf ), nor a wrapper over Linux isolation primitives (e.g. firejail , AppArmor, etc.). gVisor is also not a VM in the everyday sense of the term (e.g. VirtualBox, QEMU).

items.name: musql
items.description: SQLite-compatible database with a JIT; 300× C SQLite, 1000× Turso.

readme.excerpt:
SQLite-compatible SQL, accelerated by columnar storage and a JIT compiler.

musql pairs a new storage format optimized for columnar execution with just-in-time (JIT) compilation. The format stores columns contiguously; the JIT turns supported query paths into native machine code at runtime. Filters and aggregates work directly over those columns, reducing row decoding and interpreter overhead. In a 100,000-row read benchmark, a filtered count ran about 300× faster than C SQLite and nearly 1,000× faster than Turso . See performance for the full comparison and measurement scope.

Use it as an embedded database through database/sql , import existing SQLite data, or replicate a database across nodes that need to work independently.

A lot of good ideas start on someone else's site. Ask an agent to rebuild one from a link or a screenshot and it makes one pass, calls it done, and misses. It can't see the motion or tell how far off it is.

reanimate records the original, rebuilds it in your code, then records the copy the same way and compares the two. Each round shows what's still off, so the agent keeps going until the numbers match. You end up with a close starting point to make your own.

The skills CLI asks which agents to set up; add -a claude-code to skip the question. Then, in Claude Code, say what you want, where it is and where it should go:
features: Record. It films the reference in a headless browser at a fixed viewport and frame rate: a video, numbered frames, every CSS and Web Animati
Spec. One row per element per property: start, duration, from → to, easing, stagger. A row with a "?" means the frames haven't been read yet
Verify. It films the copy the same way, compares timing, easing and pixels, and makes side-by-side sheets.
Repeat. It fixes the biggest difference and films again, usually 2 to 5 rounds. Whatever still doesn't match after 5 is listed in its report
Pages behind a login, YouTube and Loom can't be recorded directly; hand it a screen recording.
Physics springs are fitted from their overshoot and settle time, not read from the source.
Workers are seeded and traced, but their own clocks run in real time. Canvases inside iframes need the iframe's own URL.
When a clone can't reproduce the reference's random generator, particles are compared with a blurred mismatch (density, colour, motion) inst

items.name: google-colab-cli
items.description: A CLI for interacting with Google Colab runtimes

readme.excerpt:
A command-line interface for Google Colab. Provision high-performance CPU, GPU, and TPU runtimes, execute local code, manage remote files, and orchestrate automated cloud pipelines — directly from your terminal.

Designed to support seamless developer productivity, headless automation, and AI agent integrations.

Instant VM Provisioning: Spin up CPU, GPU (T4, L4, G4, H100, A100), or TPU (v5e1, v6e1) runtimes in seconds. Robust Code Execution: Run local Python scripts, Jupyter Notebooks ( .ipynb ), or piped stdin code; launch interactive REPLs or raw TTY console shells. Ephemeral Job Runner ( colab run ): Provision a fresh VM, execute a local script with forwarded arguments, retrieve output files, and automatically tear down the runtime in a single command. Activity-Based Liveness: Sessions stay alive as long as the kernel is active, with the Colab backend automatically maintaining liveness. Seamless Workspace Automation: Mount Google Drive, authenticate Google Cloud Platform (GCP) credentials, and install dependencies with high-performance uv package management. State & Log Archival: Inspect local session states or export interactive history logs to standard Jupyter Notebooks, Markdown, or structured JSONL.

items.name: nsh
items.description: Native Shell is a native UI framework for iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, Linux and the web, built in Rust.

readme.excerpt:
Build once, native everywhere. Native Shell is a native UI framework for iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, Linux and the web, built in Rust. It unifies components, state, logic and API, with app-owned visual design and platform rendering: native views on iOS, Android, macOS, Windows and Linux, HTML on the web, GPUI in GPUI apps, character Cells in a terminal, with the platform's own text, input and interaction (a menu is a popup on the desktop and a sheet on a phone). Write the whole app in Rust, its screens in TSX, or combine both with shared Rust components.

Package it as a standalone app on every platform, or embed it in an existing one. On the same engine, apps load TSX modules at run time — plugins, features, UI generated by AI — delivered as signed packages and run in a sandbox the host configures.

Native views and interaction, with an app-owned design: NSH shares components, state and APIs across platforms, while the app controls colors, typography, spacing, shapes and motion. nsh/base provides the behavior and accessible structure of common controls such as Button , Checkbox and Switch ; apps and community libraries give them a look. Platform modules expose capabilities specific to their platforms, such as the mobile system tab bar.
features: Write apps in Rust, TSX, or both, and render with each platform's own UI, sharing the same reactive engine,
Give your app its own look: NSH provides the primitives, Tailwind classes, a theme and an unstyled UI foundation
Embed in existing native apps alongside components such as maps and web views, or package as standalone apps
Deliver TSX screens at run time with signed packages and host-controlled sandbox capabilities.
Iterate with TSX hot updates, headless tracing and a single Rust-built nsh CLI for building and packaging.

items.name: oink
items.description: Your computers, working as one. Share keyboard, mouse, trackpad, clipboard, drag and drop and audio across Macs and PCs.

readme.excerpt:
Oink, short for "Oink Is Not only a KVM", is modern software that builds a peer-to-peer sharing network across multiple Windows and Mac computers. Use the keyboard, mouse and trackpad of any device to control any nearby device, with the same native feel everywhere; play the audio of several devices through the speakers or headphones connected to one of them; share the clipboard and drag and drop between devices; discover devices on the local network automatically; all traffic is encrypted by default.

Get installers and matching source from GitHub Releases.

- Mac: Apple silicon (arm64), macOS 14.2+; Intel (x64), macOS 14.2+ (untested) - Windows: x64, Windows 10 version 1809 (build 17763) or later, or Windows 11. Windows 10 versions before 22H2 are untested. Windows 10 LTSC (such as LTSC 2019 / LTSC 2021) does not include the WebView2 Runtime; install the Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime (Evergreen) first: https://developer.microsoft.com/microsoft-edge/webview2/
